body.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every \(P\in\Delta^{15}\) with \(q_0,q_1>0\), and every real \(\Delta\),
\[
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing.
\]
These equivalences are the positive-margin corollary of \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\).  The weak fiber corresponds, by the conditionalization and mixing maps in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\), exactly to this note's measure-valued conditional reformulation of the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham two-period equations.  This comparison does not assert equality with the published fixed-reference or Lebesgue-density program.  The strict fiber from \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) is an additional subclass of the weak fiber from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\), not a second comparator match.  The weak certificate has exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3\times3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate has sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6\times6\) common-Hankel-range blocks.  The forward and reverse legal-kernel maps, including arbitrary atomic, absolutely continuous, or mixed probability laws on \((0,\infty)\), are those proved in the all-laws theorem.

body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\), \(P\in\Delta^{15}\), \(q_0,q_1>0\), and \(\Delta\in\mathbb R\).  The two displayed finite-lift equivalences follow directly from \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\), whose observable-law hypothesis is only \(P\in\Delta^{15}\).  Thus the feasibility sets are equal to the independently model-defined fibers; they are neither definitions of those fibers nor outer approximations.  The positive-margin condition is not used in this first step.

For the weak comparator statement, \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\) applies because \(q_x>0\) for each \(x\in B\).  Its forward map normalizes the finite measure \(h_xd\mu\) by \(q_x\), and its reverse map mixes the two conditional probability laws with weights \(q_x\) and recovers \(h_x\) by Radon--Nikodym derivatives.  The lemma proves, equation by equation, that both maps preserve all sixteen path probabilities and the unconditional APE.  Hence the weak legal fiber equals this note's measure-valued conditional reformulation of the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham two-period equations.

The source-scoped content of \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\) concerns the published conditional nonnegative-function program and its grid computations.  It supplies no premise replacing an arbitrary probability measure by a measure absolutely continuous with respect to a fixed reference measure.  Moreover, the conditionalization and mixing maps just invoked preserve atoms and singular components.  Therefore the proved equality is only with the note's measure-valued reformulation; it does not imply equality with the published fixed-reference or Lebesgue-density program.

By \(\mathrm{def{:}strict\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\), every member of \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) satisfies every weak restriction and additionally satisfies strict initial-assignment and feedback positivity.  Thus \(\mathcal M_+(c)\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\), and the strict fiber is an additional subclass rather than a second comparator match.

Finally, the variable and block counts are immediate from the two lift definitions and are also part of the all-laws theorem.  For the weak lift there are forty entries \(m_{s,k}\), eight entries \(a_s\), and eight entries \(b_s\), totaling fifty-six; its matrix inequalities are the eight \(3\times3\) blocks \(H_s\) and eight \(4\times4\) blocks \(K_s\).  The strict lift adds the eight entries \(t_s\) and the eight \(6\times6\) blocks \(R_s\), totaling sixty-four variables.  The all-laws theorem supplies the stated forward joint-response construction and reverse Radon--Nikodym legal-kernel reconstruction for arbitrary probability measures on \((0,\infty)\).  This proves every part of the corrected corollary.
